justification: Real numbers from a serial `verify-page.mjs --drafts` run: Lighthouse 93/100/100/100 (all four categories clear the round's 90 floor, performance up from round 1's 91), zero console errors, zero broken links, mobileOverflowPx 0. The round-1 blocker is resolved: the writer replaced the two-column 'Situation'/'Use' comparison table with a five-item bulleted list ('Choosing chaining, open addressing, or Dictionary<TKey,TValue>' section). I confirmed directly in the mobile-light and mobile-dark part-19/20 screenshots (390px) that every item, including the previously-hidden 'Custom key type: override GetHashCode/Equals together, from immutable state, or use a record,' is now fully visible with normal text wrapping in both themes -- no truncation, no horizontal scroll, no reliance on the `.fade-r` edge-fade affordance. This is a strict improvement over a table that was unreadable on the majority (phone) viewport per WRITER_GUIDE.md's own framing. I did a fresh full pass on the rest of the page. Both hand-written SVG diagrams remain fully legible at 390px in both themes: Figure 1 (chaining vs. open-addressing collision resolution, mobile-light/dark part 3-4) and Figure 2 (buckets[]/entries[] parallel-array layout with a worked example, part 9) render crisp strokes, readable labels and correctly themed captions with no clipping. Heading hierarchy is unchanged and correct: one h1, h2 sections matching the on-page structure, and the single h3 ('Building HashMap<K,V>: real chaining, not pseudocode') properly nested. All four exercises (Remove, amortized resize, struct-key prediction, find-the-bug) collapse their solutions behind a working `<details><summary>Show solution</summary>` toggle -- verified directly in mobile screenshots for exercises 1, 3 and 4, and exercise 2's collapsed state is consistent with the same component used throughout. Code/prose rhythm is unchanged from round 1: worked example, then prose walking the exact lines, repeated through nine sections; some sections re-paste the full HashMap<TKey,TValue> class verbatim so each snippet compiles standalone under run-code.mjs, producing long scroll-only-code stretches (e.g. parts 5 and 7) -- this is a site-wide convention already noted as non-scoring in round 1, and it is unchanged here. No new defects were introduced by the table-to-list conversion or found elsewhere on a fresh pass. The one remaining item is the same non-article, integrator-owned Lighthouse performance profile flagged in round 1 (bfcache restoration blocked, elevated FCP/LCP/max-potential-FID, unused CSS) -- performance still clears the 90 floor at 93 and improved slightly since round 1, so this does not affect the score.
